title: 3.5.22 Lab: Destructure 3 Fields From an Object
description: Unpack three fields in one statement, use the bare names, and rewrite a function to destructure its parameter. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Build an object with three fields
steps.instructions: Create an object with at least three properties, for example a title, a cost, and a quantity.

steps.title: Unpack into three variables
steps.instructions: Destructure three of its properties into variables in one statement, using braces on the left of the equals sign.

steps.title: Use the bare names
steps.instructions: Use the three variables (no dot, no object name) to build and print a sentence.

steps.title: Destructure a parameter
steps.instructions: Write a function called describe that takes one options object and destructures two or more of its keys directly in the parameter list (the keys are your choice), then returns a string built from the bare names.

requirements.title: object destructuring used
requirements.description: Unpacks at least three fields with a brace pattern.
requirements.hint: Put the names you want in braces on the left of the equals sign, and the object on the right. The names must match the keys.

requirements.title: describe destructures its parameter
requirements.description: describe has a brace pattern as its one parameter. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)
requirements.hint: Put the braces and key names right in describe's parentheses, instead of one ordinary parameter name: function describe({ title, quantity }).

requirements.title: the three unpacked names are used in a printed sentence
requirements.description: After the unpack, each of the three names is used on its own (no dot, no object name) inside console.log, or in a variable that is then printed. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)
requirements.hint: Use each unpacked name on its own, like title + " costs " + cost, inside console.log or in a sentence variable you then print. A name copied into a variable nobody prints does not count.

requirements.title: describe unpacks its parameter and uses the names
requirements.description: describe takes one object, unpacks two or more of its keys in the parameter list, and returns text built from them: changing the values of at least two of those keys changes the text. Help: 3.5.20 (Destructuring in a Parameter List)
requirements.hint: describe takes ONE object and unpacks two or more keys with braces in its parameter list. Build the returned string from those names, so new values give new text.

checks.expr: typeof describe === 'function' && describe.length <= 1 && (() => { const m = /^[^(]*\(\s*\{([^}]*)\}/.exec(String(describe)); if (!m) return false; const keys = m[1].split(',').map((x) => x.trim().split(/[\s:=]/)[0]).filter((k) => /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(k)); if (keys.length < 2) return false; const kinds = [[(j) => 3 + 2 * j, (j) => [1000 + j, 0]], [(j) => String(3 + 2 * j), (j) => [String(1000 + j), '0']], [(j) => 'Word' + 'ABCDEFGH'[j % 8], (j) => ['Other' + j]]]; return kinds.some(([b, alts]) => { try { const base = () => { const o = {}; keys.forEach((k, j) => { o[k] = b(j); }); return o; }; const r0 = String(describe(base())); if (r0 !== String(describe(base()))) return false; return keys.filter((k, j) => alts(j).some((a) => { const o = base(); o[k] = a; return String(describe(o)) !== r0; })).length >= 2; } catch (e) { return false; } }); })()
checks.fail: describe should take one object, unpack two or more of its keys with braces in the parameter list, and build the text it returns from those names: give it new values and the text should change.

requirements.title: the unpacked names are printed by code that runs
requirements.description: A console.log that runs prints a sentence built from each of the three unpacked names, and no printed line says undefined. Text typed in, typeof, and a print that never runs do not count. Help: 3.5.19 (Destructuring)
requirements.hint: Print a sentence built from the three names you unpacked, like title + " costs " + cost, on a line that runs.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined or NaN: one of the names you unpacked is not a key of the object. Every name in the braces must match a key exactly.
The unpacked names are not all printed by code that runs. Build a sentence from each of them, title + " costs " + cost, and print it.
